ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ABC = \angle BAC = 45^\circ$, point $P$ lies on $AB$, $AD \perp CP$, $BE \perp CP$, with the feet of the perpendiculars being $D$ and $E$ respectively. Given that $DC = 2$, what is the length of $BE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} \\
Given that $\angle ABC=\angle BAC=45^\circ$, \\
thus, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$ and AC=BC, \\
since $\angle DAC+\angle ACD=90^\circ$ and $\angle BCE+\angle ACD=90^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle DAC=\angle BCE$, \\
In $\triangle ACD$ and $\triangle CEB$, \\
hence, $\triangle ACD \cong \triangle CEB$ (AAS), \\
therefore, $BE=CD=\boxed{2}$.

Since $\angle DAC + \angle ACD = 90^\circ$ and $\angle BCE + \angle ACD = 90^\circ$, it follows that $\angle DAC = \angle BCE$. In $\triangle ACD$ and $\triangle CEB$, hence $\triangle ACD \cong \triangle CEB$ (AAS), therefore, $BE = CD = \boxed{2}$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure, A is located at the upper right, B is located at the lower left, and C is located at the lower right, forming triangle ABC; P is on side AB. The oblique line through C and P passes through E, P, D, C, and the right-angle marks in the figure show that AD is perpendicular to CP, and BE is also perpendicular to CP; D and E are the feet of the perpendiculars respectively.

Then reason: It is known that ∠ABC = ∠BAC = 45°, so the third angle of triangle ABC, ∠ACB = 90°, and AC = BC. Because AD ⟂ CP and BE ⟂ CP, △ACD and △CEB are both right triangles. Also because CD and CE are both on line CP, and ∠ACB = 90°, there is ∠BCE + ∠ACD = 90°. In right triangle ACD, ∠DAC + ∠ACD = 90°, so ∠DAC = ∠BCE. Therefore △ACD and △CEB have one pair of corresponding acute angles equal, and the hypotenuses AC = BC, so the two right triangles are congruent. The corresponding sides BE = CD. It is known that DC = 2, so BE = 2.
